meet verb

see someone, get together

also meet up, get together, meet with, see someone

classical

Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: ibi M. Mārcellum … convēnī
Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit
Traupman 17, 344: meet, tr. and intr.

conveniō, convenīre, convēnī, conventum

verb, fourth conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

meet (someone); come together

Transitive of meeting a person (aliquem convenīre); intransitive of people coming together in one place.

Other words

  • congredior, congredī, congressus sum — meet with, talk with

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.24.2: cum eō saepe congressus (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With cum: to meet someone, usually to talk.

Examples

  • itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus

    so no one who wanted to see me has ever yet found me busyCic. Sen. 32

  • cum ab Epidaurō Pīraeum nāvī advectus essem, ibi M. Mārcellum, conlēgam nostrum, convēnī eumque diem ibi cōnsūmpsī, ut cum eō essem

    when I had come by ship from Epidaurus to the Piraeus, I met our colleague Marcus Marcellus there, and spent the day there so as to be with himServius Sulpicius in Cic. Fam. 4.12.1

See also meet, pleased to meet you, visit, spend.
